title: Radiocarbon dates
what: Where archaeologists have dated remains by carbon-14: bones, charcoal, seeds, shell, from about 35,000 sites.
how: About 170,000 dates gathered from many regional databases by the p3k14c project. Each is a radiocarbon age, so it is calibrated here, against IntCal20 north of the equator and SHCal20 south of it, and placed at its median calendar age; then counted by 1° square and 250 years, back to 10,550 BCE. The squares are deeper where there are more dates, on a scale against the busiest shown. They show where dates have been measured, not how many people lived: some regions, Europe and North America above all, have been dug and dated far more than others. The database fuzzes its locations to protect the sites, so a square is as close as it goes. Picking a place lists its sites, and “How was a date here found?” carries one of its dates across the curve again.
